small_guidance:
- Add autotune configs with larger BLOCK_HW (512, 1024) and num_warps=8/16, since OC=64 is fixed and the inner GEMM tile (OC×BLOCK_HW) can scale up to better amortize weight loads.
- Cache weights once per kernel: hoist `tl.load` of the full weight tensor (OC×IC×KH×KW = 64×8×3×3 = 4608 floats) outside the spatial loop using a single load, and reuse across all BLOCK_HW tiles — currently weights are re-loaded per (ic,kh,kw) which is fine but a one-shot load may be better.
- Try `num_stages=4` with BLOCK_HW=256 to better hide the x_ptr loads from global memory across the 9 kh/kw iterations.
large_guidance:
- Switch to a persistent kernel where each program processes one (n, oc_tile) and streams over the entire OH×OW with a row-wise sliding window: load IC×KH input rows into shared memory/registers once per output row, reuse across KW shifts. This cuts the redundant input loads (currently each input pixel is loaded ~KH×KW=9 times per oc tile).
- Alternative: implicit-GEMM with channels-last (NHWC) input layout — pack IC=8 into the K dimension contiguously so a single 128-bit load fetches all 8 channels for one spatial location, then do a tl.dot(BLOCK_M=OC=64, BLOCK_N=BLOCK_HW, BLOCK_K=IC*KH*KW=72) using tensor cores (fp16 accum or tf32) for the matmul, with ReLU+HardSwish fused in epilogue.
- Consider splitting the output spatial tile into 2D (BLOCK_OH × BLOCK_OW) instead of 1D BLOCK_HW so the KH/KW sliding window has better input reuse and avoids the `ih = oh + kh` divergence across row boundaries within a tile.
